trust_decision.summary: Whether the session user may modify (delete image, patch fields, upload/remove pronunciation) the profile of the userId taken from the URL path or the patched body; decided in ProfileServiceImpl (owner or super user). At the pinned commit only setProfileImage decides it; the webapi controller checks only that a session exists, and content-hosting writes run under a blanket security advisor, so the service check is the only gate.

landing_point.why: The summary names profile image deletion; DELETE /users/{userId}/profile/image is the handler, and it checks only for a non-null session user before calling profileService.removeProfileImage(userId).

fix_sites.entry_point: PATCH /api/users/{userId}/profile (ProfileController.patchProfile), also internal call from removePronunciationRecording; public API ProfileService.saveUserProfile
POST /api/users/{userId}/profile/image (ProfileController.putProfileImage); already guarded, refactored into the shared helper
DELETE /api/users/{userId}/profile/pronunciation; adds the missing session check
POST image / GET image details / DELETE image: redundant null-user checks removed (fix.diff:302-337)
GlobalExceptionHandler maps SecurityException to 403 for all webapi routes

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about deleting a profile image; PATCH of text fields and the pronunciation recording are neighbouring features, and a solver who adds a path-userId check in patchProfile considers PATCH done without noticing that the JSON patch can rewrite /id in the body that saveUserProfile trusts.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Super users must still remove/update other users' images, profiles and recordings, and any logged-in user must still read other users' profiles, images and pronunciation (roster views); putting an owner-only check on getUserProfile/getProfileImage or dropping the isSuperUser branch breaks these. removePronunciationRecording internally calls getUserProfile and saveUserProfile, so a check that rejects these internal calls breaks owner removal.

target user in the JSON-patched body field 'id' (PATCH -> saveUserProfile(profileBean.id))
pronunciation write via body field 'audioBase64' in PATCH
no session at all (DELETE pronunciation had no session check)

Pattern A is weak: every closed sink lives in one service file (ProfileServiceImpl), and setProfileImage already shows the exact check as a template, so 'routes of one concept fall together' is likely. The main lever is the PATCH body 'id' variant plus the pronunciation feature being argued as a neighbouring feature.
